newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close sharply higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed sharply higher on Sunday in very active trading as investors moved money from short-term deposits to bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.24 pct to 102.42
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.14 pct to 101.52.
Volume was a high 195 million shekels.

"The bond market looks very good. Prices rose sharply and yields fell today for no evident reason. The most active players in the market are mutual funds and provident funds," said Shahar Gazit at Batucha Securities and Investments.

"The main reason for today's rise is that the public is taking out money from short-term bank deposits and moves it to mutual funds which specialise in bonds," said a trader at I.B.I. Investment House.
"New money comes into the market and yields are falling. Yields on long unlinked bonds fell sharply to only 4.25 percent," Gazit said.
"Unlinked bonds and Makams were also rising as investors show interest in all bonds," the I.B.I. trader said.
Yields on the Makam (for one year) fell from 13.79 percent on Thursday to 13.68 percent.
Traders said that dollar linked bonds were also rising following the recent rise of the U.S. currency.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
